key_insight: The paper generates realistic polycrystalline microstructures by learning a compact anisotropic power-diagram representation with a $C_4$-equivariant flow-matching model.
engineering_relevance: This enables scalable, rotation-consistent synthetic microstructure generation for materials design, simulation, and data augmentation when EBSD data are limited or costly.
method: Represent microstructures as anisotropic power diagrams for compact geometry.
Use graph neural network flow matching to synthesize microstructures from noise.
Add $C_4$ equivariance and training-free guidance to enforce rotational symmetry and steer outputs toward target morphologies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports qualitative generation of microstructures resembling a copper weld, cast metal slab, 3D-printed stainless steel, and heterogeneous lamella titanium.
watch_item: The method’s usefulness depends on the fidelity of the geometric representation and guidance objectives; quality may be sensitive to how well they capture real microstructure statistics.
paper_title: $C_4$-Equivariant Flow Matching on Anisotropic Power-Diagram Graphs for Microstructure Generation
